update_log: Baseline initialization of major Biosphere Reserves (focusing on UNESCO MAB status) and high-frequency Ramsar Wetlands for Geography Static GK.

biosphere_reserves.name: Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: The first biosphere reserve in India (established 1986).

biosphere_reserves.name: Gulf of Mannar
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: First marine biosphere reserve in South and South-East Asia.

biosphere_reserves.name: Nanda Devi
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: Includes the Valley of Flowers National Park.

biosphere_reserves.name: Sundarbans
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: Largest contiguous mangrove forest in the world.

biosphere_reserves.name: Nokrek
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: Part of the Garo Hills; famous for Citrus indica (Indian wild orange).

biosphere_reserves.name: Pachmarhi
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: Located in the Satpura Range; often called the 'Queen of Satpura'.

biosphere_reserves.name: Similipal
biosphere_reserves.key_fauna: Royal Bengal Tiger, Asian Elephant, Gaur
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: Gets its name from the abundance of red silk cotton trees growing in the area.

biosphere_reserves.name: Khangchendzonga
biosphere_reserves.key_fauna: Snow Leopard, Red Panda, Musk Deer
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: One of the highest ecosystems in the world; added to UNESCO MAB network in 2018.

biosphere_reserves.name: Cold Desert
biosphere_reserves.key_fact: Includes Pin Valley National Park and Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary.

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Chilika Lake
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: India's first Ramsar Site (along with Keoladeo); largest coastal lagoon in India; famous for Irrawaddy dolphins.
high_yield_ramsar_sites.montreux_record_status: Removed (Was added in 1993, removed in 2002 after successful restoration)

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Keoladeo National Park
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Formerly Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary; wintering ground for Palaearctic migratory waterfowl.
high_yield_ramsar_sites.montreux_record_status: Active (Due to water shortage and unbalanced grazing regime)

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Loktak Lake
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Largest freshwater lake in Northeast India; famous for floating islands (phumdis) and Keibul Lamjao National Park.
high_yield_ramsar_sites.montreux_record_status: Active (Due to ecological problems raised by the Ithai Barrage)

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Wular Lake
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Largest freshwater lake in India; fed by the Jhelum River.

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Harike Wetland
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Formed by the confluence of the Beas and Sutlej rivers.

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Vembanad-Kol Wetland
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Longest lake in India; famous for the Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race.

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Bhoj Wetland
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Consists of two contiguous human-made reservoirs (Upper and Lower Lake) in Bhopal.

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Deepor Beel
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: Permanent freshwater lake in a former channel of the Brahmaputra River; critical elephant corridor.

high_yield_ramsar_sites.name: Tsomoriri
high_yield_ramsar_sites.significance: High-altitude lake representing the only breeding ground outside of China for one of the most endangered cranes, the Black-necked crane.
